scopeEditor.info: Grant access per resource: tick the operations (Create / Read / Update / Delete) this role allows on each one. "Full access" grants everything. Optionally narrow a clause to specific owners with the row-level data filters under it.
scopeEditor.empty: No clauses yet — click "Add clause" below
scopeEditor.addClauseHelp: Add another clause. Each clause is an independent grant; access is the union of all of them.
scopeEditor.fullAccessHelp: Grant every operation on every resource (the owner default). Uncheck to grant specific permissions.
scopeEditor.advancedHint: Advanced: resource:cruds[:type] (e.g. records:rs:patient — the "s" letter grants sensitive/PHI reveal for that record type; omit it to keep fields masked). profiles:c/u/d also accepts a principal qualifier — profiles:u:self (only the credential's own profile) or profiles:c:usr_ followed by a user id (one named principal). Also accepts custom action verbs.
scopeEditor.validationNoClauses: At least one scope clause is required
scopeEditor.validationNoActions: Clause {n}: grant at least one permission
scopeEditor.validationBlankAction: Clause {clauseN}, action {actionN}: must be a non-blank string
scopeEditor.dataScopeHelp: Narrow this clause to rows owned by specific scopes — for example scope "org", value "org_acme". Leave empty to apply to every row in the context. A clause can filter on at most two scopes; multiple filters must all match. Use scope "*" to state a default for every scope this clause doesn't name explicitly. A value can also be a matcher instead of a literal — "$'{{' any '}}'" (any value present in this scope), "$'{{' under.self.userId '}}'", or "$'{{' under.self.scope.NAMESPACE '}}'" (values whose immediate parent is your own in that namespace — NAMESPACE can be this row's own scope or another one on the clause, e.g. an "org"-matcher on a "client" row) — pick one from the value field's suggestions.
scopeEditor.dataScopeIncludeNull: Also include rows with no value in this scope
scopeEditor.validationDataScopeNamespace: Clause {clauseN}: a filter scope must be 2–32 characters, start with a lowercase letter, and use only lowercase letters, digits, - or _.
scopeEditor.validationDataScopeReserved: Clause {clauseN}: "{namespace}" is reserved and can't be used as a filter scope.
scopeEditor.validationDataScopeDuplicate: Clause {clauseN}: the "{namespace}" scope is filtered twice — combine the values into one filter.
scopeEditor.validationDataScopeNoValues: Clause {clauseN}: add at least one value, or enable "include rows with no value".
scopeEditor.validationDataScopeTooMany: Clause {clauseN}: a clause can filter on at most {max} scopes.
scopeEditor.capabilitiesHelp: Bounded effects that reach across an app context, which the permission matrix above can't express. Only capabilities your own session can grant are offered here — the platform refuses a save naming one your session doesn't itself hold.
scopeEditor.capability.memberLifecycle: member-lifecycle — create and remove identities in your tenant
scopeEditor.capability.delegateMint: delegate-mint — mint a scoped API key bound to a different principal than your own
keys.title: Scoped API keys
keys.subtitle: Short-lived, scope-limited ssk_live_* / ssk_test_* keys bound to a user + access profile. Use for agents, CI tooling, and per-team-member bots.
keys.empty: No scoped keys yet. Create one to bind an agent or service account to a specific AccessProfile.
keys.emptyForEnv: No scoped keys in this environment. Switch environments in the tenant selector to see keys in the other environment, or create one here.
keys.revokeConfirmBody: You're about to revoke {keyName} (bound to user {userId}).
keys.revokeConfirmWarning: This takes effect within ~5 minutes — the Rust authorizer's policy-cache window. Anything currently using this key will start receiving 401 errors once the cache flushes.
keysWizard.title: Create scoped key
keysWizard.basics.envCaption: The key will be prefixed ssk_{env}_* and scoped to your {env} tenant.
keysWizard.bind.delegateMintNotice: Binding this key to someone other than yourself requires the delegate-mint capability. If your session doesn't hold it, the mint fails at the final step with a 403 — pick yourself instead, or ask an owner to grant delegate-mint to your role first.
keysWizard.bind.emptyHumans: No human users yet. Invite someone from the Members page first.
keysWizard.bind.emptyServices: No service principals yet. Click "Create service principal" above.
keysWizard.servicePrincipal.title: Create service principal
keysWizard.servicePrincipal.subtitle: Service principals are users with type=SERVICE and no email — used for agents, CI bots, and any non-human identity.
keysWizard.servicePrincipal.externalIdHe: Your system's identifier for this service. Used for idempotent lookups.
keysWizard.context.contextHelper: The app namespace within your tenant. Create one via POST /v1/app-contexts if your list is empty.
keysWizard.context.profileExists: AccessProfile exists for this (user, context) pair
keysWizard.context.profileExistsDetailSc: {count, plural, one {# scope clause} other {# scope clauses}}
keysWizard.context.profileMissingDetail: A key needs an AccessProfile to bind to. Click "Create profile" to define one inline.
keysWizard.inlineProfile.title: Create AccessProfile
keysWizard.inlineProfile.subtitle: Binding {principalId} to context {contextId}. The profile defines which actions the scoped key (and any future tokens bound to this user-in-this-context) will be permitted.
keysWizard.review.intro: Confirm the details below. After you click Create the raw key is shown ONCE — copy it before closing.
keysWizard.confirmation.copyOnce: Copy this key now — it won't be shown again.
keysWizard.confirmation.cacheWarning: New keys take up to ~5 minutes to start authorizing requests — the Rust authorizer's policy-cache window. Once that elapses you can test the key against the Vectros API.
keysWizard.confirmation.idempotentDetail: A scoped key with this (user, context, name) tuple already exists. The raw key cannot be re-disclosed — if you've lost it, revoke this one from the Keys list and create a new one with a different name.

logs.subtitle: Inspect API call history for the active tenant. Sourced from CloudWatch Logs Insights — request and response bodies are never logged.

logs.empty: No log entries found in this time window.
logs.emptyHint: Try widening the time range or clearing filters.
logs.truncated: Results truncated at {limit}. Narrow the time window or add filters to see all entries.
logs.resultCount: {count, plural, =0 {No entries} one {# entry} other {# entries}}
logs.contextHelp: Activity is shown across every app context by default. Pick a context to narrow the view to it.
logs.timeRangeInvalid: Start time must be before end time.
logs.keyIdInvalid: Use only letters, digits, hyphens, or underscores (max 64).
usage.title: Usage & credits
usage.subtitle: Your account's consumption for the current billing period: credits against your plan, read metering, and the live/test and per-context breakdowns.
usage.error: We couldn't load the usage report. Please try again.
usage.readsSubtitle: Two axes: read (GET) calls, and total response bytes egressed across all surfaces (reads, search results, and document downloads).
usage.contextsSubtitle: The finest granularity usage is attributed at. Context metrics roll up into their environment, which rolls up into the account totals.
usage.estimateNote: Storage is an in-period estimate; final billing runs at the end of the cycle. Credit values are rounded down to whole credits.
usage.contextConfinedNotice: This credential is confined to a single app context. The Used figures for Reads and Data out below read 0 because no per-context breakdown exists for those two — it does not mean no calls were made (their overage and overage-credit figures still narrow correctly). The credit balance shown above may also overstate what's actually available for this context: only the consumed and left-over figures narrow here — the account-wide ceiling does not.
access.shared.propagationNotice: Permission changes take effect within ~5 minutes (the Rust authorizer's policy-cache window).
access.shared.discardConfirm: You have unsaved changes. Are you sure you want to leave?
access.contexts.title: App contexts
access.contexts.subtitle: An app context is a namespace you define to group access profiles and roles. You usually only need the default {defaultContextId} context — add more when you have separate apps or environments with different permission models.
access.contexts.empty: No app contexts yet. The default {defaultContextId} context should exist — if you see this, something's gone wrong with provisioning.
access.contexts.redirecting: You have one app context. Opening it…
access.contexts.createDialog.title: Create app context

access.contexts.createDialog.idInvalid: Must be 3–31 chars: lowercase letter prefix, then lowercase letters, digits, or dashes.
access.contexts.editDialog.title: Edit app context
access.contexts.deleteConfirm.title: Delete app context {contextId}?

access.contexts.deleteConfirm.bodyCounts: Right now it contains {roles, plural, one {# role} other {# roles}} and {profiles, plural, one {# access profile} other {# access profiles}}.
access.issuers.title: Trusted issuers
access.issuers.subtitle: Third-party identity providers your users can sign in through. Registering a new issuer requires a provisioning-scoped credential and is done through the CLI or SDK — this page lets you review what's registered and adjust the safe, non-cryptographic settings.

access.issuers.editDialog.title: Edit issuer {issuerId}
access.issuers.editDialog.intro: The issuer URL, JWKS endpoint, required audience, and app context are set at registration and can't be changed here — shown below for reference. Delete and re-register the issuer (via the CLI or SDK) to change one of those.
access.issuers.editDialog.subClaimHelper: The claim in the identity provider's token that carries the subject identifier. Defaults to "sub".
access.issuers.editDialog.emailClaimHelp: The claim that carries the subject's email, used for invite matching. Defaults to "email".
access.issuers.editDialog.selfSignupHelp: A first-time caller from this issuer who names one of these signup types is created automatically, without an invite, bound to the paired role. A policy can never target a role with elevated permissions.
access.issuers.editDialog.saveError.frie: Could not save your changes. Refresh and try again.

access.profiles.subtitle: Bindings of principals (users or scoped keys) to a permission source — either a referenced role or inline scope clauses.
access.profiles.empty: No profiles yet. Click "Create profile" to bind a principal to a permission set.
access.profiles.sourceInline: Inline ({count, plural, one {# clause} other {# clauses}})
access.profiles.editor.principalIdHelper: A user (usr_…) or API key (key_…) principal. Suffix: letters, digits, underscores, dashes.
access.profiles.editor.principalIdInvali: Must be usr_SUFFIX or key_SUFFIX. Suffix: letters, digits, underscores, or dashes only.
access.profiles.editor.principalPickerHe: Pick the user to grant access to. To bind an API key instead, type its key id (key_…).
access.profiles.editor.grantMultiRole: Inherits every permission from {count} composed roles: {roleIds}.
access.profiles.editor.grantFull: Full access — every action in this context.
access.profiles.editor.grantNone: No permissions yet — choose a role or add at least one action.
access.profiles.editor.sourceSwitchConfi: Switching sources discards the current draft. Continue?
access.profiles.editor.roleRefHelper: Profile inherits this role's scopes. Updates to the role propagate automatically.
access.profiles.editor.multiRoleNotice: This profile is composed of {count} roles: {roleIds}. Editing a multi-role composition isn't supported in this admin app yet — use the CLI (vectros access grant --role, repeatable) to change it, or switch this profile to inline scope clauses to replace the composition entirely.
access.profiles.editor.cloneMultiRoleDis: Can't clone a profile composed of multiple roles — not supported in this admin app yet. Use the CLI (vectros access grant --role, repeatable) instead.
access.profiles.editor.identityOverrides: Optionally override the ownership scopes this principal stamps in this context. Leave blank to inherit from the principal's base identity. The user's audit identity is always preserved. A principal can carry at most two scopes (org, client, and any custom scopes combined).

Identity overrides can't be set from this sign-in: granting one requires a credential that already holds the identity value being granted, and this one doesn't hold any. Any values below are shown for reference only — sign in as an account that holds an identity, or use a root API key, to change them.
access.profiles.editor.identityOverrideE: Override a custom ownership scope by namespace — for example namespace "group", value "eng-team". Org and client use the fields above.
access.profiles.editor.identityOverrides: A principal can carry at most {max} scopes (org, client, and custom combined). Remove one to add another.
access.profiles.editor.identityOverrideN: Namespace must be 2–32 characters, start with a lowercase letter, and use only lowercase letters, digits, - or _.
"{namespace}" is reserved and can't be used as a scope namespace.
Use the Org ID / Client ID fields above for the "{namespace}" scope.
The "{namespace}" scope is already set. Each namespace can appear once.
access.profiles.editor.identityOverrideV: Enter a value for this scope, or remove the row.
Value must be 1–128 characters, start with a letter or digit, and use only letters, digits, - or _ (no ":").
access.profiles.cloneDialog.title: Clone access profile
access.profiles.cloneDialog.materializeH: When off, the cloned profile keeps the role reference — role updates propagate. When on, the role's current scopes are copied into the clone as inline scope clauses, decoupling it from future role changes.
access.profiles.cloneDialog.identityOver: This profile's identity overrides won't be copied to the clone: this sign-in doesn't hold a matching identity to grant them. Everything else will still be cloned.
access.profiles.deleteConfirm.title: Delete access profile for {principalId}?
access.profiles.deleteConfirm.body: This removes the binding in {contextId}. Scoped API keys bound to this profile will start returning 401 within ~5 minutes (the authorizer's policy-cache window). This cannot be undone.
access.profiles.deleteConfirm.bodyBlocke: This profile has identity overrides this sign-in doesn't hold. Removing them requires a credential that already holds the identity being removed — sign in as an account that holds it, or use a root API key, to delete this profile instead.
